🔑 Key — abbreviations

VSR
Voltage Sensitive Relay — auto-connects batteries when the source is charged enough to share
MPPT
Maximum Power Point Tracking — the smarter charge-controller type; squeezes the most out of panels/turbines
PWM
Pulse Width Modulation — the simpler, cheaper controller type; fine for small panels
DC-DC
DC-to-DC charger — steps voltage up or down to charge one battery bank from another
AGM
Absorbed Glass Mat — sealed lead-acid battery; maintenance-free
LiFePO4
Lithium Iron Phosphate — the lithium bank; the system's primary storage
SOC
State of Charge — how full a battery is, as a %
AWG
American Wire Gauge — wire thickness; lower number = thicker wire
PV
Photovoltaic — solar panels
MPPT vs PWM, plain English: MPPT is the brainy one — it constantly hunts for the sweet spot where the panel makes the most power, so you harvest more, especially in mixed light. PWM is the simple on/off switch — cheaper, fine for small setups, leaves some power on the table.
Catches wind and sun out west — shares the surplus east only when its own battery is full.

Wire run

WB1 → WB2 · 70 ft · 8 AWG underground
Step-up booster at the WB1 end (15.6V) · VSR-gated — carries raw source power. The smart charging happens at the far end.
Collects WB1's surplus plus its own wind and sun — then gates power toward the hub when charged.

🔋 Battery

  • 400Ah flooded (Duracell)

💨 Wind In

  • Smaraad 24V turbine sold as 1000W
  • → green SYNARAD MPPT wind controller boost from 6V

☀️ Solar In

  • 2× 100W Werchay bifacial (one brand-new Nov 2026) + portable 100W trickle → Renogy 40A MPPT DC-DC
The 40A also takes WB1's VSR feed on its DC input — sits at the WB2 end so it senses WB2's battery cleanly.

🚪 Gate Out

  • VEVOR 140A VSR (installed Oct 30) — 13.3V on / 12.6V off, AUTO mode
Chargers live at the battery they charge. VSRs live at the source they sense. The wire in between just carries dumb power.

Wire run

WB2 → Hub · ~100 ft · 8 AWG underground
VSR-gated source feed. The REGO 50A #2 lives at the hub end — takes the saggy wire voltage and boosts it to proper charge voltage for the lithium, with short output leads.
Banks the power in two battery chemistries, bridges AGM → lithium, inverts to AC, and feeds the barn.
